title: With Asian Games Gold Secured, India Hockey Eyes Los Angeles 2028
excerpt: India's men defended their Asian Games hockey title with a 5-1 win over Malaysia, the women ended a 44-year wait against China, and both squads have booked direct tickets to LA 2028.
body:
• India's men's hockey team defended its Asian Games gold with a 5-1 win over Malaysia — the country's first-ever successful title defence and its fifth Asian Games men's hockey gold.
  • Captain Harmanpreet Singh scored twice in the final and finished the tournament with 12 goals as its leading scorer.
  • The women's team beat China 1-0 to end a 44-year wait for Asian Games gold, their first since 1982; both squads have now qualified directly for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.
  • No qualifiers needed: with nearly two years to LA 2028, head coach Craig Fulton plans to use the Hockey India League to scout young talent and build a fresh Olympic squad.

A Gold Defended, a Drought Ended

India's men's hockey team achieved something no Indian side had managed before: defending its Asian Games gold. The Harmanpreet Singh-led side beat Malaysia 5-1 in the final at the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium in Aichi-Nagoya, adding to the 2023 triumph to win back-to-back titles for the first time and securing a direct ticket to the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics. A day earlier, the women's team ended a 44-year wait for Asian Games gold with a 1-0 win over China — also earning direct Olympic qualification.

https://x.com/TheHockeyIndia/status/2106678186830373122

Captain Harmanpreet Singh opened the scoring in the 11th minute from a penalty corner and added another in the 57th. Malaysia briefly equalized through Shello Silverius, but Jugraj Singh restored India's lead in the 23rd minute before Hardik Singh (42nd) and Shilanand Lakra (54th) sealed a commanding final. Harmanpreet's brace took his tournament tally to 12 goals, making him the competition's leading scorer and the first Indian men's captain to win two Asian Games golds.

Context and Background

The men's campaign was not without turbulence. India won all five group matches, then edged Pakistan 4-3 in a dramatic semifinal after the arch-rivals fought back from 3-0 down to level at 3-3. The team had faced scrutiny coming into the Games, but produced its most complete performance in the final. India's Asian Games men's hockey golds now stand at five — 1966, 1998, 2014, 2023 and 2026 — with the class of 2023 and 2026 becoming the first back-to-back winners.

For the women, the gold carried four decades of weight. India had not topped the Asian Games podium since 1982, with runner-up finishes in 1998 and 2018, and narrowly missed the Paris 2024 Olympics after finishing fourth at Tokyo 2020. Ranked eighth in the world, India upset fourth-ranked China in the final, with Lalremsiami scoring the winner in the 10th minute. Midfielder Hardik Singh hailed the women's achievement, saying it stood "above ours" given the 44-year gap.

Impact and Analysis

The direct qualification is the real prize. India no longer has to navigate the Olympic qualifier gauntlet, which means the next 22 months can be spent on preparation rather than survival. Veteran midfielder Manpreet Singh, a four-time Olympian who won his third Asian Games gold, said the team can now work on fitness and specific weaknesses instead of worrying about qualification.

"The Asian Games was a very important tournament for us because from here we have directly qualified for LA. We can work on ourselves, identify the areas where we need to improve and go to LA better prepared."

— Manpreet Singh, India midfielder

Head coach Craig Fulton is already planning for Los Angeles, and his comments point to regeneration. The South African coach said India will assess the next generation after the Hockey India League, with strong talent in the India A and Under-21 squads, and "choose new squad, and start afresh from there." With several seniors in their thirties, the next cycle will blend the proven core — Harmanpreet, Hardik, Jugraj — with youth developed through the domestic league pipeline.

Diaspora Angle

For the Indian diaspora in the United States, this Olympic cycle is personal. Los Angeles 2028 will be the first time many Indian-American fans can watch India chase hockey gold on home soil, without a trans-Pacific flight. The women's team's revival adds to the story: a squad that missed Paris now arrives in LA with Asian Games gold, and both teams will carry the expectations of one of the most passionate sporting diasporas in the world.

What's Next

The immediate focus is the Hockey India League, where Fulton will scout for Olympic-cycle talent over the next two to three months. Then comes the long build: a deliberate two-year preparation plan — fitness blocks, structured competition, squad selection — designed to end India's wait for an Olympic hockey gold that stretches back to Moscow 1980.
